title: Filter decision — the input-filter gate's record of whether an inbound message reached the engine
description: Written into _report/state.json under the "filter" key by scripts/filter_gate.py. `code` and `route` are the closed vocabulary declared by reference/filter_signals.json's `categories` list (t1); both admit null for the pass-through case, where nothing was filtered so there is no category to report. `reason` is a separate closed vocabulary explaining WHY a message passed through (or was forced through), independent of the category vocabulary used when a message is filtered.

filtered.description: true if the gate stopped the run before the engine; false if the message reached (or will reach) the engine.

input.description: The exact input path the gate was given — unmodified, so a filtered message can be identified and replayed (C6).

code.description: The matched filter category, or null when the message was not filtered. Deliberately SCREAMING_SNAKE like open_items[].code, but a disjoint set of values.

route.description: Where a filtered message should go, or null when the message was not filtered. Deliberately disjoint from open_items[].route and routing.recommendation, so a consumer can never mistake a filtered message for a routed-but-undrafted case.

evidence.description: Short verbatim signal that drove the decision (a header value or matched phrase).

override.description: true when --no-filter (or a recorded screen.override) forced the message through despite matching a filter category.

reason.description: Short machine token for why a pass-through happened. Null when the message was filtered.
